text:
alex: quick sync — i sketched a lightweight idea to help attribute short-lived burst costs to tenants without blowing up tracing cardinality. calling it the 'telemetry-lease' header. TL;DR: edge proxies emit a tiny 8-12 byte token that encodes tenant id shard + lease window (very short-lived). ingest expands it to a billing bucket.

maria: can you paste the token layout? curious how you avoid PII leakage or tenant enumeration.

alex: sure, rough proto: `Telemetry-Lease: v1;shard=0x1a;wnd=60;sig=0x3f` — shard is 8 bits, wnd is seconds, sig is a 16-bit MAC. no tenant ids in the token. the shard maps to tenant buckets in an internal lookup (one-to-many).

tyler: looks promising. tradeoffs? how does this interact with sampling and late enrichment?

alex: tradeoffs — positive: constant size header so low cardinality, edge-only generation reduces latency. negative: we depend on a lookup service to map shards -> tenants at ingest; that lookup needs caching and rotation when commits change. if a request needs exact tenant attribution (billing accuracy), we'd fall back to full enrichment path (late lookup using billing keys) for sampled traces or higher-value requests.

jin: what about cross-region requests and replay? token wnd needs to account for clock skew, otherwise lease will expire before ingest.

alex: agreed. plan: encode wnd as max-age (e.g., 60s) and allow +/- 5s tolerance at ingest. for replayed traffic we mark tokens as stale and route them to a conservative billing bucket.

maria: how does this affect query/analytics? if we only have shard buckets, customers will see coarse billing until we reconcile with late-enriched data, right?

alex: correct. UX: near-real-time cost surface is per-shard (good for burst alerts). nightly reconciliation job reconciles shard tallies with canonical tenant attributions for invoicing. we keep both numbers in dashboards (shard-rt vs reconciled-invoice).

tyler: ops implications? cache invalidation model for shard->tenant mapping?

alex: mapping store is append-only per deployment, rotates every few hours. ingest caches mapping in memory with TTL=5m and a background refresh. on cache-miss we query mapping service (fast path). on mapping-change we emit a small audit event for reconciliation.

ops-bot: deploy:edge-proxy/1.14.0 rolled out to 50% (canary) in us-west-2 - watch `edge.telemetry.lease.*` metrics.

jin: curious about security — MAC key storage and rotation. we must ensure a compromised key doesn't let someone forge tokens to claim billing.

alex: plan: sign with KMS-backed symmetric key per-region. rotation window 24h; we accept tokens signed with current or previous key to allow grace. audit logs for signature verifications fail.

maria: does this change sampling decisions at the edge? e.g., prefer sampling traces where tokens map to high-spend shards?

alex: good point. we can bias sampling by shard weight. keep sampling config centralized and push to proxies. sampling bias metadata stays out of token to keep token small.

tyler: do we need a proto change to ingest schema? minimal: add `lease_shard` and `lease_wnd` fields to envelope root so downstream knows this came via lease path. also `lease_untrusted` boolean for stale signatures.

alex: yep — ingest schema additions only, default to null. no change to trace/span schema otherwise.

jin: operational fallback if mapping service is down — we should tag events as `lease_unknown` and route to a holding queue to avoid data loss.

alex: agreed. fallback: write to hot-hold SQS-like buffer for 1 hour; worker replays once mapping service recovers. metrics increment `edge.lease.buffered` and `ingest.lease.replayed`.

maria: sounds reasonable. one last ask — add a short simulation to verify cost skew and reconciliation delta before rolling. we should know worst-case delta if mapping is stale or keys rotated aggressively.

alex: will do. action items: 1) alex to post cohort sim and token spec in a short RFC doc, 2) eng-platform to add ingest schema fields + buffer path, 3) infra to provision mapping cache + KMS keys, 4) devex to wire up dashboard split (shard-rt vs reconciled). ping me if you want to join a quick 30m sync. :calendar:  

tyler: i can join. jin too. assign a lead for the RFC pls.

alex: i'll lead the RFC. posting doc later today: https://go.internal/rfcs/telemetry-lease-v1 (draft).

maria: thanks — nice compromise between latency and cost fidelity. :+1:

ops-bot: note: created ticket INF-2689 (telemetry-lease impl) assigned to alex.
